name: Kesar Da Dhaba
why_it_matters: Set up by Lala Kesar Mal in Sheikhupura (now Pakistan) in 1916; relocated to Amritsar after Partition. Now run by the fourth generation. The dal makhani simmers on wood fire in a copper pot for 8-12 hours — Nehru and Lala Lajpat Rai are on the historical guest list.
insider_tip: Skip the menu — order the thali with dal makhani, mah ki dal, lachha paratha and phirni. Cash only and no AC; arrive before 1pm or after 8pm to dodge the queue down the lane.
signature_address: Chowk Passian, near Telephone Exchange, Golden Temple Outer Circle, Amritsar 143006

name: Bharawan Da Dhaba
why_it_matters: Started in 1912 by a group of brothers — 'bharawan' literally means 'of the brothers' in Punjabi. The Town Hall original sits opposite the Municipal Corporation, a 5-minute walk from the Golden Temple. Punjabi vegetarian cooking pre-Partition, served the same way for over 110 years.
insider_tip: The malai lassi here is dessert, not a drink — order a half-glass and a kulcha-thali alongside. They open from 7am for early gurudwara crowds.
signature_address: Opposite Town Hall, Hall Bazaar, Amritsar 143001

name: Brothers' Amritsari Dhaba
signature_dish: sarson da saag with makke di roti
why_it_matters: Started in 2001 by the elder brother of the Bharawan Da Dhaba family — same lineage, more table space, walking distance from the Golden Temple. The cleaner, larger sibling that handles spillover Town Hall crowds.
insider_tip: When Bharawan Da Dhaba's 100-deep wait kills your morning, walk two minutes down to Brothers — same family recipes, faster turnaround.
signature_address: Town Hall, near Golden Temple Out Road, Amritsar 143006

name: Ahuja Milk Bhandar
why_it_matters: A two-by-three-foot stall next to Hindu College pouring the same recipe since the 1950s — clay-cup lassi crowned with malai and a fingerful of butter. Featured on Highway On My Plate as their pick for India's best lassi.
insider_tip: Order half-glass first — the malai layer is meal-thick. They sell out the first batch by 11am; afternoon lassi is fine, morning is what locals come for.
signature_address: Near Hindu College, Inside Lohgarh Gate, Amritsar 143006

name: Gian Chand Lassi Wale
area: Katra Sher Singh, opposite Regent Cinema
signature_dish: peda lassi (curd churned with peda, no sugar)
why_it_matters: Set up in 1921, now over a century old — the Golden Temple lassi joint locals call simply 'Gian di Lassi'. The peda lassi swaps sugar for crushed peda churned into the curd; thick enough to eat with a spoon.
insider_tip: There are two adjacent shops with the same name — the original is the one on the right as you face Regent Cinema. The shop closes by 8pm so this is a daytime stop.
signature_address: Katra Sher Singh, Opposite Regent Cinema, Amritsar 143006

name: Bhai Kulwant Singh Kulchian Wale
why_it_matters: A four-seat kulcha shop tucked into the lane behind the Golden Temple — flaky stuffed kulchas baked tandoor-fresh and finished with a knob of butter. Clay tandoor visible from the street; the order moves faster than the queue suggests.
insider_tip: Sit at the inner bench, not the front — the tandoor heat and the wafting butter make it the standing ritual. Eat there; takeaway kulchas lose their crackle in 10 minutes.
signature_address: Bazar Bikaneria, Near Golden Temple, Katra Ahluwalia, Amritsar 143006

name: Crystal Restaurant
why_it_matters: Opened in 1935 on Cooper Road, a 10-minute drive from the Golden Temple — Amritsar's pre-Partition fine-dining address. Three generations of the same family have kept the Amritsari fish recipe and the chandelier-and-velvet ambience intact.
insider_tip: The Cooper Road original is a different beast from the newer Crystal at Mall of Amritsar — book the original for the linen-tablecloth experience, not the mall outlet.
signature_address: Crystal Chowk, Cooper Road, Queens Road Area, Amritsar 143001

name: Gurdas Ram Jalebi Wala
why_it_matters: Opened in 1956, now run by the third generation. Hot jalebis fried in pure desi ghee from a copper kadhai facing the street. The shop is so identified with the corner that the junction itself is now called Jalebi Wala Chowk.
insider_tip: Eat the jalebi standing — fresh from the syrup it shatters; bagged-up, it gets soggy fast. Cash only, open till 11pm.
signature_address: Jalebi Wala Chowk, Katra Ahluwalia, near Golden Temple, Amritsar 143006
